name: Elizabeth Warren
role: U.S. senator from Massachusetts (2013–present); 2020 presidential candidate
summary: Warren is a progressive Democrat whose politics centre on curbing corporate and financial power: she created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, backs Glass-Steagall, antitrust break-ups, a wealth tax, Medicare for All and worker representation on corporate boards. She favours expanded legal immigration, abortion and LGBTQ+ rights, gun licensing, a Green New Deal and cuts to the defense budget, while supporting NATO and Ukraine aid.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said in the 2019 debates and on NPR that she is 'with Bernie on Medicare for All' and her campaign plan backs a public program covering all Americans.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted yes on raising the federal minimum wage in 2014, on $15 in March 2021 and on a $17 amendment in April 2025.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed an annual 2% tax on net worth between $50 million and $1 billion plus a 6% rate above $1 billion, and promoted it on air in 2019.

unions-good.rationale: Her workers plan aims to rebuild union power (repeal of right-to-work authority, PRO Act), and on the Senate floor in 2025 she called an order stripping federal workers' union rights union-busting.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Introduced the 21st Century Glass-Steagall Act with McCain, Cantwell and King and she set up the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

strong-leader.rationale: Told the Senate in 2026 that a war begun without Congress's consent must not be allowed to continue, and says no president is above the law.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted yes on the 2013 Manchin-Toomey background-check amendment; her plan adds federal licensing and an assault weapons ban.

rehabilitation.rationale: Would double grant funding for prison education and rehabilitation and favour treatment over incarceration for substance use.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted yes four times on the 2022 bill repealing the Defense of Marriage Act and protecting recognition of marriages.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted against the 2019 bill banning taxpayer-funded abortions and the 2019 born-alive bill.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Her housing plan funds down-payment help for formerly redlined communities and strengthens enforcement against redlining.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Says 'we need to expand legal immigration' and her plan raises annual refugee admissions to at least 175,000.

free-trade.rationale: Says trade is good only when it helps workers and families, and rejects deals written for multinationals and the ISDS provisions.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted against a 2013 amendment barring further greenhouse-gas regulation and against approving Keystone XL.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Called tariffs an important tool in trade policy but not by themselves a long-term solution.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposed $2 trillion of federal investment in green research and manufacturing for American-made products.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Pledges to protect tribal sovereignty and self-determination, requires the free, prior and informed consent of the Tribal Nation concerned for major projects, and would recognise tribes' inherent jurisdiction over their territory.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Her Accountable Capitalism plan has workers at large corporations elect at least 40% of the board.

school-vouchers.rationale: Opposes diverting public dollars through vouchers or tuition tax credits.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Calls to renew the fight against segregation and discrimination in schools, and condemns redlining that denied Black families federal housing subsidies.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted against approving the Keystone XL pipeline in 2014 and 2015.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said at the July 2019 debate that the biggest problem in Washington is corruption, and has a plan titled End Washington Corruption.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says immigrants are every bit as much a part of America as those born here, calls for equal treatment of LGBTQ+ people, Muslims and racial minorities under law.

separated-powers.rationale: Says a president cannot start a war without Congress's consent and that no president is above the law, with the Justice Department answering to the people rather than the president.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Would ban permanent replacement of strikers and set a high bar for government intervention in strikes.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Voted to admit Montenegro, Finland and Sweden to NATO and for a 2023 bill requiring Congress's consent to leave it.

death-penalty.rationale: States 'I oppose the death penalty' and calls on Congress to abolish it.

minority-language-support.rationale: Supports Native language revitalization and immersion programs in K-12 funding and fostering English learners' home languages.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Criticised cuts to humanitarian aid and USAID, listing restoring them among uses of public money.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Says 'it's time to get rid of the Electoral College' so that presidential candidates must ask every American for their vote.

collective-defense.rationale: Voted yes on a 2017 resolution reaffirming NATO's Article 5 and on the accession of Montenegro, Finland and Sweden.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Plan states no president is above the law and that Congress should clarify presidents can be indicted, including for obstruction.

ban-cartels.rationale: Wants to break up Amazon, Google and Facebook, and told the Senate antitrust laws exist to break up trusts and protect competition.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Wants labor standards central to every trade agreement and Paris-agreement membership as a condition.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Original cosponsor of the Equality Act and says religious liberty should not be used to shield bigotry.

elective-rulers.rationale: Wants presidents chosen by a national popular vote so candidates must ask every American for their vote.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Said on CNN in 2014 that Social Security shouldn't be privatized and her plan expands it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Calls corruption Washington's biggest problem and wants to end corporate PAC money, ban lobbyist fundraising and require supermajority shareholder approval for corporate political spending.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Original cosponsor of the Equality Act and campaigns for LGBTQ+ equality, including a nationwide ban on conversion therapy.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Would reinstate Education Department protections for transgender students, create a third gender marker, and cover gender-affirming care.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Says Muslims are one of the most diverse communities in the country and have always been a vital part of the American story.

racial-franchise.rationale: Pledges to stop racist voter suppression and says the right to vote is a fundamental right.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argues that concentrated economic power buys political power (antitrust speech) and that great fortunes should pay back; her tax plan targets concentrated wealth.

free-public-college.rationale: Calls for tuition-free public two-year and four-year colleges, with the federal government partnering with states.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Supports the PRO Act and a move to sectoral bargaining so workers in an industry bargain together.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Plans to cancel up to $50,000 of student loan debt for 42 million people.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Wants Congress to reduce or eliminate mandatory minimums and give judges discretion.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Says she has led the fight to repeal the federal provision that lets states pass right-to-work laws.

indigenous-internal-justice.rationale: Calls for a full Oliphant fix and expanded tribal criminal jurisdiction, and a fund to help tribal courts hire public defenders.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: Her foreign policy plan commits to working with partners to crack down on tax havens.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Proposes public financing as the sole way to fund elections via constitutional amendment, a ban on lobbyist bundling and an end to corporate PAC money.

notes: Sources: her 2020 campaign plan pages (words), the two July/September 2019 debates, Voteview Senate roll calls 2013-2026 (record), Congressional Record floor speeches and a hearing, and CNN/NPR transcripts via MediaSum. Where she has a vote on a statement the answer rests on the vote alone; the plans answer only statements without a vote. The 2020 plans are campaign pledges, so they are used only where she has no record on the point. Views: Medicare for All and the wealth tax were campaign positions held since 2018; trade (voted for the 2015 trade enforcement bill, against its 2016 final version) is treated as words only because the votes are on enforcement, not free trade. Searched in the local corpora theme by theme: economy (wages, taxes, unions, banking, antitrust, student debt), liberty (guns, drugs, sentencing, surveillance), society (abortion, LGBTQ+, race, immigration, religion), world (NATO, Ukraine, Israel, Iran and war powers, trade, defense budget, aid), government (campaign finance, voting rights, Electoral College, courts, presidential power), ecology and technology. Nothing found from her on secularism or church-state questions, nationalism and national culture, secession, regional autonomy, revolution or political violence as a general question, one-party rule, or monarchy; those stay null, so she fails the uncertainty rule on those lines. A search for her views on abolishing police and prisons, sex work, all-drug legalisation, hate-speech laws, encryption, rent caps and nuclear power found no stated position.
